node.title: Re: Overriding built-in function works only via import()?
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Why does the first code work, while the second doesn't?

[http://shop.oreilly.com/product/9780596004927.do|The Camel] (🐪, Chapter 11) to the rescue:

Overriding Built-in Functions ... it's the assignment of a code reference to a typeglob that triggers the override, as in *open = \&myopen. Furthermore, the assignment must occur in some other package; this makes accidental overriding through typeglob aliasing intentionally difficult.

And looking at git history, the corresponding language was in [doc://perlsub] [https://perl5.git.perl.org/perl.git/blob/a0d0e21ea6ea90a22318550944fe6cb09ae10cda:/pod/perlsub.pod#l139|as early as perl-5.000]. So the behavior appears to be quite intentional.

And BTW, here's another short way to do what you want that doesn't use [doc://subs]:

BEGIN { package Foo; *main::readpipe = sub {"Foo"} } print `xyz`; __END__ Foo
